passages.title: What should you do if you get lost in a forest?
passages.text:
Every year, many hikers and mushroom pickers get lost in forests. Most of them are found within 24 hours, especially if they follow a few simple rules. The first and most important rule is to stop walking as soon as you realise you are lost. Many people panic and keep walking, which makes it much harder for rescuers to find them.

If you realise you are lost …
• Stay calm and sit down. Try to remember how you got there.
• If you have a phone, call the emergency number. Save the battery by turning off apps you don't need.
• Make yourself easy to see. Wear bright clothes or hang something colourful on a tree.

If you have to spend the night outside …
• Find or build a shelter, for example under a large tree with low branches, and use leaves to keep warm.
• Don't drink water from rivers or lakes unless you can boil **<u>it</u>** first.
• Blow a whistle three times in a row. It is the international signal for help and can be heard much further away than a voice.
